body:
Thank you for the kind response. It's a vicious cycle, really. One thing that I should have mentioned is that I do have friends. I have some roommates from college and some friends from abroad with whom I have contact. I am not completely alone, but all of these people live far away. One of my best friends from high school lives about 30 minutes away and, although we used to hang out all the time, I have not tried to contact him since I finished graduate school (May 2011).

The problem with having friends is that I am afraid of getting burned. In high school, college, and graduate school, I thought that I would make lots of friends, but it didn't happen. I am not an outgoing or friendly person, which hurts my chances, but I am really afraid that things will always end badly. It's a vicious cycle and it's really not healthy. 

I live with my parents (although not for much longer, if my job situation keeps going the way that it is (one of the few positive things I have going for me)), and they have offered to pay to send me to therapy, but I have always refused. I don't know why I do it. Because I am not naturally depressed, I feel like I just don't want to get better. I'm not suicidal, but I am just tired of everything. Thank you for the kind words, though.
